column1: One layer of one app's dock. Three of them share this table, told apart by `app`, `user` and `standard`: the app's own dock, which an app ships as an exported document and a developer authors; the site's arrangement of it, curated by a Workspace Manager and applying to everyone; and one person's own, applied last and winning. A dock belongs to an app, so arranging ERPNext's rail does not touch frappe's -- and a layer is addressed by app plus user rather than by user alone. Same shape at all three, because the rows are identical and the parent is what says whose they are; see `Custom Sidebar`, which layers a sidebar the same way in a table of its own.
column2: One layer of one app's dock. A dock belongs to an app, so arranging KodeERP's rail does not touch frappe's -- and a layer is addressed by app plus user rather than by user alone.
